principles.statement: Ozone-Studio owns its lifecycle: build, restart, verify, and hand-back are learned procedures, not tribal memory in any agent's session.
principles.rationale: The host must be rebuildable and restartable by ANY agent (or the human) by following the stored methodology — no agent may become a load-bearing process holder.

principles.statement: The canonical data store is target/release/zsei_data — the operator's standard launch is `cd target/release && ./ozone-studio`. Working directory determines the data directory; a launch from any other directory silently uses a DIFFERENT store. Never run the host from elsewhere, and never edit store files under a running host (recreate via the API instead).
principles.rationale: Two launch cwds created two divergent live stores (2026-09-15: 12-task vs 41-task split). One canonical store, matching the operator's actual habit, prevents the class entirely.

principles.statement: Build with constrained parallelism: `cargo build --release -j 2`. The host machine has 7.6GB RAM and a 4G swapfile; unbounded jobs caused real OOM restarts.
principles.rationale: A build that kills the machine takes the host down with it; -j 2 is the proven-safe setting.

principles.statement: Every restart is followed by verification before work resumes: /health (healthy, uptime reset), coordination tasks still queued, agent registry repopulating, jurisdiction region detected.
principles.rationale: A restart without verification hides silent failures (empty registry, lost queue, failed self-heals) behind a seemingly healthy process.

principles.statement: Agents never hold the host process. The human (or a supervisor designated through Ozone tasks) runs the host; agents REQUEST restarts as tasks and verify after.
principles.rationale: An agent holding the host makes the host's life cycle depend on that agent's session — the opposite of the connect model.

heuristics.name: Restart Request Protocol
heuristics.description: Need a restart (new binary, config change)? Create a host task titled '[host-ops] restart requested — <reason>', then notify the operator channel (monitor feed + notes). The operator restarts from the repo root; agents verify afterward.
heuristics.when_to_apply: After merging any change to src/ that alters host behavior (new endpoints, registry changes, boot logic).
examples: New /mcp/call endpoint merged → task '[host-ops] restart requested — McpCall endpoint live' → operator: pkill ozone-studio, then ./target/release/ozone-studio from repo root → agents verify /health uptime reset + new endpoint answers.

heuristics.name: Pre-Restore Task Snapshot
heuristics.description: Coordination tasks with an assignee survive restarts as queued (reconciliation exempts them). Before ANY restart, confirm the queue: POST /task/list — queued coordination work is expected to reappear; anything else queued will honestly become 'interrupted'.
heuristics.when_to_apply: Immediately before requesting or performing a restart.
examples: Tasks 7-11 queued → restart → task/list shows 7-11 still queued (agent work survived); an orchestrator mid-flight task would show interrupted instead.

heuristics.name: Post-Restore Verification Ladder
heuristics.description: In order: (1) curl /health → healthy + uptime < 60s; (2) GET /pipelines/remote → agents re-register within ~30s heartbeats; (3) GET /mcp/tools → ozone-shared-context self-registered within a minute of any agent session; (4) POST /task/list → coordination tasks queued; (5) boot log shows jurisdiction region detection. Only after all five is the host 'verified up'.
heuristics.when_to_apply: After every host start, without exception.
examples: 2026-09-15 restart: health ok, zcode re-registered in 30s, tool self-registered, tasks 7-11 queued, 'Jurisdiction region: auto-detected' in log — verified.

heuristics.name: Build-then-Swap
heuristics.description: cargo build --release -j 2 FIRST; only if it exits 0 does the restart happen. The running process is never killed for a binary that failed to build.
heuristics.when_to_apply: Any restart that exists to deploy new code.
examples: Executor fix built clean (exit 0) → restart; a failed build leaves the old binary serving.

decision_rules.condition: Host is down or unhealthy and no operator is present.
decision_rules.action: Agents report the outage through the monitor feed and wait; they do NOT spawn long-lived host processes from their sessions. The operator runs ./target/release/ozone-studio from the repo root.
exceptions: A designated supervisor task explicitly assigns a named agent to run the host for a defined maintenance window.

decision_rules.condition: A merged change requires a restart to take effect.
decision_rules.action: Follow Restart Request Protocol: build clean first, then task + notify, then verify with the full ladder after the operator restarts.

decision_rules.condition: Repeated OOM or machine instability during build.
decision_rules.action: Confirm -j 2 is set; check swap (swapon --show, 4G expected); if still unstable, stop and escalate to the operator — do not retry with higher parallelism.

decision_rules.condition: Data appears missing after restart (tasks, containers).
decision_rules.action: Check the working directory first: repo-root launch uses ./zsei_data; a launch from target/release uses target/release/zsei_data. Mismatched cwd is the most common cause of 'lost' data.
